tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not only she arrived late, but she also forgot her keys.
Seldom the café opens before seven on Sundays.
Never the neighbours had complained about the noise.
No sooner had the kettle boiled than the toast burned.
Under no circumstances the children will stay home alone.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Fronted "not only" needs inversion: "Not only did she arrive late…".

Tip: If "not only" sits at the start, treat it like a question for the auxiliary: did/does/had + subject.

FALSE — Needs "Seldom does the café open…".

Tip: Negative frequency words (seldom, rarely, never) at the start almost always trigger inversion.

FALSE — Fronted "never" needs "Never had the neighbours complained…", not subject–verb order.

Tip: With past perfect after "never", move "had" before the subject.

TRUE — "No sooner…than" with past perfect inversion is the classic pattern here.

Tip: Pair "no sooner" with "than" (not "when") and invert: "had + subject".

FALSE — Needs "Under no circumstances will the children stay…".

Tip: Modal + subject swaps after a negative prepositional phrase at the front.
tasks.solution_overview: These openers look formal, but the test is mechanical: a negative or restrictive phrase at the front usually forces auxiliary–subject order. Scan each line for that swap first, then check the correlative word (than/when) if "no sooner" or "hardly" appears.

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Hardly had the film started when the fire alarm went off.
Rarely we see such clear skies in November.
Little did the guests realise how long the queue would be.
Not only did the recipe look simple, but it also tasted great.
Seldom the library stays open past nine on weekdays.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Hardly had…when…" is the standard inverted past-perfect pattern.

Tip: After hardly/scarcely/barely, prefer "when" (or "before"), not "than".

FALSE — Needs "Rarely do we see…".

Tip: No auxiliary visible? Add do/does/did and place it before the subject.

TRUE — "Little did…" correctly inverts after a restrictive opener.

Tip: "Little" meaning "not at all" behaves like a negative fronting word.

TRUE — Fronted "not only" takes inversion, and "but also" keeps the second clause parallel.

Tip: Check both halves: inversion after "not only", then a matching "but also" clause.

FALSE — Requires "Seldom does the library stay…".

Tip: "Seldom" + present simple → does/do before the subject.
tasks.solution_overview: Task 2 drills the core set: hardly, rarely, little, not only, seldom. Correct lines already invert; wrong ones leave ordinary subject–verb order after a fronted negative. Fix those by inserting or moving the auxiliary.

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Under no circumstances should this door be left unlocked overnight.
No sooner the bus pulled away than Marta realised she had left her bag.
Never has the school cancelled sports day for such a light drizzle.
Scarcely the match had begun before the referee stopped play.
At no time the coach authorised a change of kit colour.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Negative adverbial + modal inversion is clean: "should this door be left".

Tip: After "under no circumstances", expect will/should/can before the subject.

FALSE — Needs "No sooner had the bus pulled away than…".

Tip: "No sooner" almost always pairs with past perfect and inversion of "had".

TRUE — "Never has the school cancelled…" correctly inverts present perfect.

Tip: Keep the participle after the subject: Never + has/have + subject + past participle.

FALSE — Needs "Scarcely had the match begun…".

Tip: Scarcely/hardly/barely fronting → had + subject + past participle.

FALSE — Needs "At no time did the coach authorise…".

Tip: "At no time" is a full negative fronting phrase; invert like a question.
tasks.solution_overview: Focus on stock fronting phrases: under no circumstances, no sooner, never, scarcely, at no time. If the phrase is negative and sits first, the next word should be an auxiliary, not the subject.

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only after the rain stopped did the picnic become possible.
Not until the train doors closed did Alex notice the wrong platform.
Hardly the hikers had reached the ridge when fog rolled in.
On no account may visitors feed the animals in this enclosure.
Nowhere in the guidebook does it mention the Monday closure.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Only after…" inverts the main clause: "did the picnic become".

Tip: With only + time clause, leave the time clause alone and invert the main clause.

TRUE — "Not until…" likewise inverts only the main clause.

Tip: Do not invert inside the "not until" clause itself.

FALSE — Needs "Hardly had the hikers reached the ridge when…".

Tip: Hardly + past perfect: had before the subject.

TRUE — "On no account may visitors…" is a correct formal prohibition with inversion.

Tip: "On no account" and "under no circumstances" behave the same way.

TRUE — "Nowhere…does it mention…" correctly inverts after a negative place adverbial.

Tip: Nowhere/no place at the front → does/do/did + subject.
tasks.solution_overview: Four of these already invert correctly after only after, not until, on no account, and nowhere. The odd one out is "hardly" without "had" before the subject—fix that pattern and the rest fall into place.

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: No longer does the bakery deliver to our street.
Barely had the concert begun when the lights failed.
In no way can the warranty cover water damage from floods.
Not only was the hotel full, but the next town was booked out too.
Seldom have we eaten such fresh bread from a roadside stall.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "No longer" at the front takes "does the bakery deliver".

Tip: No longer + present simple → do/does before the subject.

TRUE — "Barely had…when…" mirrors the hardly pattern.

Tip: Barely/hardly/scarcely share the same inversion + "when" template.

TRUE — "In no way can the warranty…" correctly inverts the modal.

Tip: In no way / under no circumstances / on no account all pull the modal forward.

TRUE — Fronted "not only" with "was" before the subject is right, and the second clause completes the contrast.

Tip: With be-verbs, invert be itself: Not only was the hotel…

TRUE — "Seldom have we eaten…" is clean present-perfect inversion.

Tip: Frequency negative + have/has + subject + past participle.
tasks.solution_overview: Every sentence here is already inverted. Use them as models: spot the fronted negative, confirm the auxiliary sits next, then note the correlative (when/but also) where relevant.

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: No sooner had the dishwasher finished than the sink filled again.
Rarely does a local team win away in such weather.
Not only the chef objected, but the waiters also complained.
Under no circumstances will pets be allowed in the exhibition hall.
Never the museum had displayed so many private loans at once.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Past-perfect inversion after "no sooner" plus "than" is exact.

Tip: Memorise the trio: no sooner + had + subject + than.

TRUE — "Rarely does…" correctly adds do-support for present simple.

Tip: If there is no auxiliary, invent do/does/did for the inversion.

FALSE — Needs "Not only did the chef object, but…".

Tip: Fronted not only without an auxiliary still needs did/does/do.

TRUE — Modal inversion after "under no circumstances" is correct.

Tip: will/must/should jumps before the subject after this phrase.

FALSE — Needs "Never had the museum displayed…".

Tip: Never + past perfect → Never had + subject + past participle.
tasks.solution_overview: Three lines already invert; two leave the subject right after not only / never. Mentally flip those into question order and you will see the repair immediately.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Hardly had the snow melted when another frost arrived.
Little the tourists understood about the ferry timetable.
Only when the power returned did the fridge start humming again.
Scarcely had the paint dried on the fence when rain began.
Seldom the post office updates its holiday opening hours early.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Hardly + had + subject + when is textbook.

Tip: Keep "when" (not "than") after hardly/scarcely/barely.

FALSE — Needs "Little did the tourists understand…".

Tip: Little as a fronting restrictor needs did/does/do + subject.

TRUE — Only when + clause, then invert the main clause.

Tip: Invert after the time clause ends, not inside it.

TRUE — Scarcely had…when… matches the hard/barely family.

Tip: Same skeleton for scarcely, hardly, and barely.

FALSE — Needs "Seldom does the post office update…".

Tip: Present-simple after seldom → does/do before the subject.
tasks.solution_overview: Hardly, scarcely, and only when are shown correctly; little and seldom are missing their auxiliaries. Add did/does and the pattern locks in.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not until the referee blew the whistle the players left the pitch.
Under no circumstances are bikes permitted inside the shopping centre.
No sooner had the oven preheated than the dough was ready.
At no point did the guide admit that the path was closed.
Rarely a quiet carriage stays quiet for the whole journey.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Needs "…did the players leave the pitch" after the not-until clause.

Tip: Not until + time clause → invert the main clause with did/does/do or an auxiliary.

TRUE — Be-verb inversion after "under no circumstances" is fine: "are bikes permitted".

Tip: With be, invert be itself; no extra do-support.

TRUE — No sooner + had + than is correct again.

Tip: Watch the correlative: than after no sooner.

TRUE — "At no point did the guide admit…" is solid inversion.

Tip: At no point / at no time are interchangeable triggers.

FALSE — Needs "Rarely does a quiet carriage stay…".

Tip: Rarely + present simple → does/do + subject + base verb.
tasks.solution_overview: Most lines invert cleanly. The traps are "not until" without main-clause inversion and "rarely" without do-support—both classic exam misses.

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only by booking early can we secure seats near the stage.
No sooner had the parcel arrived when the courier rang again.
Not only did traffic jam the bridge, but the tunnel closed as well.
Under no circumstances should raw chicken sit on the worktop.
Never before has the festival sold out in a single morning.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Only by…" inverts the main clause: "can we secure".

Tip: Only + prepositional phrase at the front still forces inversion.

FALSE — "No sooner" takes "than", not "when": "…arrived than the courier rang again".

Tip: Correlative pairs: no sooner→than; hardly/scarcely→when.

TRUE — Not only + did + but…as well is correctly inverted and balanced.

Tip: Keep both verbs parallel after not only / but also.

TRUE — Modal inversion after under no circumstances is right.

Tip: should/must/will before the subject after this opener.

TRUE — "Never before has…" correctly inverts present perfect.

Tip: Never before / never again behave like never for inversion.
tasks.solution_overview: Inversion is mostly done right; the subtle miss is the correlative after "no sooner". Word order can look perfect and still fail if than/when is swapped.

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Hardly had the teacher finished speaking than phones started buzzing.
Not until the keys were found did the family leave the flat.
Seldom do neighbourhood shops stay open past midnight.
On no account the intern may unlock the storeroom alone.
Little did the runners know a shortcut waited behind the hill.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Hardly pairs with "when", not "than": "…speaking when phones started buzzing".

Tip: Swap than→when after hardly/scarcely/barely even if inversion looks fine.

TRUE — Not until + clause, then "did the family leave".

Tip: Main-clause inversion only; leave the time clause in normal order.

TRUE — Seldom + do-support is correct.

Tip: Frequency negatives need do/does/did when no other auxiliary exists.

FALSE — Needs "On no account may the intern unlock…".

Tip: Move the modal before the subject after on no account.

TRUE — Little did… is a stock restrictive inversion.

Tip: Little + did + subject + base verb is the usual template.
tasks.solution_overview: Two errors here mix correlative choice (hardly…than) with missing modal inversion (on no account). Check both word order and the linking word after the fronted phrase.

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only after the laundry dried the sheets were folded and stacked.
Nowhere else will you find cherries this sweet in late summer.
Scarcely had the guests sat down when dessert appeared.
Not only did the app crash, it also wiped the draft message.
Under no circumstances the cleaner will mix bleach with ammonia.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Needs "…were the sheets folded and stacked" (or "…did anyone fold the sheets").

Tip: Only after + time clause → invert the main clause.

TRUE — Nowhere else + will + subject is correct.

Tip: Nowhere / nowhere else at the front always invert.

TRUE — Scarcely had…when… is the right pair.

Tip: Keep when after scarcely; keep had before the subject.

TRUE — Not only… with inversion is acceptable; "it also" can finish the contrast.

Tip: "But also" can appear as "it also" if the second clause still matches.

FALSE — Needs "Under no circumstances will the cleaner mix…".

Tip: will must precede the subject after this fronting phrase.
tasks.solution_overview: Only after and under no circumstances still trap people who invert late or not at all. The other three already show the target shapes—use them as anchors.

tasks.title: Task 12
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: No sooner had the curtains opened than applause filled the hall.
Rarely have gardens recovered so quickly after a late frost.
Not only was the suitcase heavy, but the zip was broken.
At no time were passengers told about the platform change.
Barely had the bakery opened when the first queue formed.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — No sooner + had + than is perfect.

Tip: Drill the correlative than until it is automatic.

TRUE — Rarely + present perfect inversion is correct.

Tip: Rarely have/has + subject + past participle.

TRUE — Not only was…but… keeps be inverted and the contrast clear.

Tip: With was/were, invert be; no do-support needed.

TRUE — At no time + were + subject is correct be-inversion.

Tip: Passive or be-main verbs invert be itself.

TRUE — Barely had…when… matches the hard/scarcely family.

Tip: Barely = hardly for inversion purposes.
tasks.solution_overview: A clean model set: no sooner, rarely, not only, at no time, barely. If your own answers miss any of these shapes, rewrite the wrong ones to match these templates.

tasks.title: Task 13
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only if the weather clears will the outdoor market go ahead.
The notice not only lists opening times but also warns about roadworks.
No sooner had breakfast ended than the day trip coaches arrived.
Hardly the ink had dried on the consent form when surgery was cancelled.
Under no circumstances are personal heaters permitted in the office.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Only if + clause, then invert the main clause: "will the outdoor market go".

Tip: Conditional "only if" at the front still triggers main-clause inversion.

TRUE — Mid-sentence "not only…but also" needs no inversion.

Tip: Invert only when "not only" is fronted; otherwise keep normal order.

TRUE — No sooner…than with past perfect inversion is correct.

Tip: Confirm than after no sooner every time.

FALSE — Needs "Hardly had the ink dried…when…".

Tip: had must sit before the subject after hardly.

TRUE — Under no circumstances + are + subject is correct.

Tip: Be-inversion after this phrase is standard in policies.
tasks.solution_overview: The key sophistication here is knowing when not to invert: mid-clause "not only…but also" is fine. The only hard fail is hardly without had-before-subject.

tasks.title: Task 14
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not until did the plumber fix the leak the floorboards were dry.
In no circumstances should leftover rice sit out overnight.
Seldom has a village fete drawn such a crowd in midweek.
No longer the tram line serves the old factory estate.
Only after did the museum reopen were tickets put on sale.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Do not invert inside the not-until clause; say "Not until the plumber fixed the leak were the floorboards dry" (or "…did the floorboards dry").

Tip: Invert the main clause only—never invert the not-until/time clause itself.

TRUE — "In no circumstances should…" is the same family as under no circumstances.

Tip: In/under no circumstances both pull the modal forward.

TRUE — Seldom + present perfect inversion is correct.

Tip: Seldom has/have + subject + past participle.

FALSE — Needs "No longer does the tram line serve…".

Tip: No longer + present simple → does/do before the subject.

FALSE — Wrong placement of did; use "Only after the museum reopened were tickets put on sale".

Tip: Keep the only-after clause normal; invert the main clause alone.
tasks.solution_overview: Advanced traps put the auxiliary in the wrong clause (not until / only after). Remember: time/condition clause stays normal; the following main clause inverts.

tasks.title: Task 15
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not only did the soup burn, but the bread went stale as well.
Scarcely had the rehearsal ended than the costume call began.
Never again will the club host fireworks without a fire marshal.
Little does the neighbourhood appreciate how quiet the park becomes at dusk.
Under no circumstances the lifeguard may leave the pool unattended.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Fronted not only + did, completed by but…as well, is acceptable.

Tip: "But also / but…as well" both work if the first half inverts.

FALSE — Scarcely takes "when", not "than".

Tip: Correlative check: scarcely/hardly/barely → when; no sooner → than.

TRUE — Never again + will + subject is correct.

Tip: Never again / never before behave like never.

TRUE — Little does… correctly inverts present simple with do-support.

Tip: Little + does/do + subject + base verb.

FALSE — Needs "Under no circumstances may the lifeguard leave…".

Tip: Modal before subject after under no circumstances.
tasks.solution_overview: Inversion looks right on the scarcely line, but the correlative is wrong. Pair that check with the modal-order miss on under no circumstances.

tasks.title: Task 16
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only when the Wi-Fi returned did the online class continue.
No sooner the suitcase was packed than the taxi horn sounded.
At no stage were residents told about the water shut-off.
Rarely do we publish the newsletter without a photo gallery.
Not only the soundtrack disappointed; the plot disappointed too.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Only when + clause, then "did the online class continue".

Tip: Invert after the when-clause finishes.

FALSE — Needs "No sooner was the suitcase packed than…" or "No sooner had the suitcase been packed than…".

Tip: No sooner requires inversion of be/had immediately after it.

TRUE — At no stage + were + subject is correct be-inversion.

Tip: At no stage / at no point / at no time are equivalent triggers.

TRUE — Rarely + do-support is correct.

Tip: Rarely do/does + subject + base verb.

FALSE — Fronted not only needs inversion: "Not only did the soundtrack disappoint…".

Tip: If not only leads the sentence, insert did/does/do before the subject.
tasks.solution_overview: Two failures omit inversion after no sooner and not only. The survivors show only when, at no stage, and rarely done properly—mirror those.

tasks.title: Task 17
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not until the fridge was emptied the movers wheeled it downstairs.
Under no circumstances may allergy medication be shared between guests.
Seldom has a community garden produced such a crop of tomatoes.
Only by rearranging the furniture can the sofa fit through the door.
Hardly had the babysitter arrived than the toddler woke up crying.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Needs "…did the movers wheel it downstairs".

Tip: Not until → invert the main clause; do not leave subject–verb order there.

TRUE — Under no circumstances + may + subject is correct modal inversion.

Tip: After this phrase, expect may/will/should before the subject.

TRUE — Seldom + present perfect inversion is correct.

Tip: Seldom has/have + subject + past participle.

TRUE — Only by + -ing, then modal inversion in the main clause.

Tip: Only by / only with / only through all invert the following clause.

FALSE — Hardly takes "when", not "than".

Tip: Even with perfect inversion, wrong correlative still fails the item.
tasks.solution_overview: Top-band items stay inside negative/restrictive inversion: not until, under no circumstances, seldom, only by, hardly. Judge each line by whether the auxiliary moved—and whether than/when is the right partner.

tasks.title: Task 18
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Under no circumstances is smoking permitted near the playground.
No sooner had the ferry docked than foot passengers streamed ashore.
Not only were tickets refunded, but free drinks were offered as well.
Seldom does a weekday market feel this crowded before noon.
Little did neighbours expect the street party to last past midnight.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Under no circumstances + is + subject is correct.

Tip: Be-main verbs invert be after this phrase.

TRUE — No sooner…than with past perfect is exact.

Tip: had + subject + than remains the gold standard.

TRUE — Not only were…but… correctly inverts were.

Tip: Plural subject → were before it after not only.

TRUE — Seldom does… is clean do-support inversion.

Tip: Frequency negative + does/do + subject + base verb.

TRUE — Little did… is the classic restrictive inversion.

Tip: Little + did + subject + base verb.
tasks.solution_overview: All five are model answers across the core triggers. Treat this task as a checklist of shapes you should be able to produce under exam pressure.

tasks.title: Task 19
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only after the gym closed members were allowed to collect belongings.
Not until the vet confirmed the results did the owners relax.
Barely had the campsite been booked when a storm warning arrived.
On no account should unfinished cakes leave the kitchen counter.
Never the caretaker had unlocked every classroom before dawn.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Needs "…were members allowed to collect belongings" or "…did members become free to collect belongings".

Tip: Only after + clause → invert the main clause.

TRUE — Not until…did… is correctly inverted in the main clause.

Tip: Keep the not-until clause in normal order.

TRUE — Barely had…when… is right.

Tip: Passive past perfect still inverts had: Barely had the campsite been booked…

TRUE — On no account should… is correct modal inversion.

Tip: should/must/may before the subject after on no account.

FALSE — Needs "Never had the caretaker unlocked…".

Tip: Never + past perfect → Never had + subject + past participle.
tasks.solution_overview: Two lines forget to invert after only after and never. The others show not until, barely, and on no account in full working order—match those repairs to the same templates.

tasks.title: Task 20
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Nowhere in the hiking leaflet does it mention the Monday trail closure.
Not only did the hostel refill the kettle, but it also left fresh towels.
Hardly had the blackout ended when the street lights flickered back on.
Under no circumstances the landlord will enter without written notice.
No sooner had the suitcases been labelled than the taxi pulled up.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Nowhere…does it mention… correctly inverts after a negative place adverbial.

Tip: Nowhere / no place at the front → does/do/did + subject.

TRUE — Not only did…but also… is fully inverted and parallel.

Tip: Match verb forms across both halves after not only / but also.

TRUE — Hardly had…when… is the standard pattern.

Tip: when after hardly; had before the subject.

FALSE — Needs "Under no circumstances will the landlord enter…".

Tip: Final check on every under-no-circumstances item: modal before subject.

TRUE — No sooner had…than… closes the set correctly.

Tip: than after no sooner; had before the subject.
highlights: Nowhere in the hiking leaflet does
tasks.solution_overview: Four model inversions and one classic miss: under no circumstances without modal–subject swap. If you catch that last pattern every time, this topic is exam-ready.
